quickStart.item_08: For an immediate emergency in Hong Kong, call 999.
quickStart.item_54: Review emergency contacts, health details, legal document locations, insurance, bank accounts, MPF, pensions, and essential liabilities.
quickStart.item_33: If someone has died, identify the executor or authorised representative and use the Hong Kong Judiciary Probate Registry and provider instructions.
quickStart.item_26: Hong Kong probate grants cover Hong Kong estate assets; overseas property may need separate administration under the relevant jurisdiction.
quickStart.item_66: Use official bank, MPF, IRD, and service-provider bereavement processes. Do not access accounts or use credentials without authority.
quickStart.item_44: Keep the export encrypted. Never store passwords, iAM Smart or eTAX credentials, authentication codes, or recovery keys in it.

legalNotes.item_32: Hong Kong has its own identity, healthcare, MPF, tax, probate, and property systems; do not apply another country's rules to Hong Kong assets.
legalNotes.item_31: HKID particulars are sensitive personal data. Record only what is necessary and share it only with organisations that need it.
legalNotes.item_33: Hong Kong public healthcare and private healthcare are distinct; eligibility and charges depend on status and service rules.
legalNotes.item_120: The Hong Kong Probate Registry explains that probate, letters of administration, or letters of administration with will annexed may be required. Hong Kong grants cover Hong Kong estate assets; overseas assets may require separate administration.
legalNotes.item_50: MPF death benefit claims are administered under the MPF system. Confirm who may claim and which documents are needed with the trustee and MPFA.
legalNotes.item_34: Hong Kong salaries tax, profits tax, property tax, and estate-duty questions depend on circumstances and relevant dates. Confirm current IRD guidance rather than relying on fixed thresholds in this organizer.
legalNotes.item_77: Official: Hong Kong health system overview: https://www.gov.hk/en/residents/health/hosp/overview.htm
legalNotes.item_79: Official: Hong Kong Judiciary Probate Registry: https://www.judiciary.hk/en/court_services_facilities/probate.html

recoveryRoadmap.description: A general checklist after a death in Hong Kong. Confirm authority, domicile, estate location, and current court and provider requirements before acting.

meta.title: Family Recovery Roadmap - Hong Kong
meta.reviewedBy: Government sources reviewed; case-specific legal and tax advice may be needed

intro.condolence: We are sorry for your loss. This checklist is intended to make the first practical steps clearer.
intro.howToUse: Register the death, identify the executor or administrator, notify relevant agencies and providers, and keep a record of each action.

startHere.0: Follow the official death-registration process and obtain the records requested by providers.
startHere.1: Locate the will and identify the executor; confirm whether a Hong Kong grant is required.
startHere.2: Notify banks, MPF trustees, insurers, employers, IRD, and other providers through their official bereavement processes.
startHere.3: List Hong Kong and overseas assets separately; confirm jurisdiction, ownership, and authority before changing accounts or distributing property.
startHere.4: Keep a log of contacts, forms, and documents supplied. Never use another person's iAM Smart, eTAX, or banking credentials.

legalFramework.0: Hong Kong Judiciary Probate Registry grants and estate administration.
legalFramework.1: The Hong Kong Probate Registry's jurisdiction is limited to estate assets in Hong Kong; overseas assets follow the applicable local process.
legalFramework.2: MPF scheme and trustee claim rules for a member's death.
legalFramework.3: IRD salaries, profits, property, and any relevant estate-duty rules.
legalFramework.4: Hong Kong identity, healthcare, and legal-document rules; seek advice for cross-border domicile or estate issues.
